timeline.label: FY2025 10-K recasts financials on two-segment structure (Healthcare & Water Technologies, Diversified Industrials) after Electronics separation.
Electronics business separation completed; DuPont retains specialty healthcare, water, and industrial materials portfolio.
Total debt reduced to roughly $3.2 billion (long-term plus current) versus higher pre-separation leverage.
Delrin divestiture to TJC closed; further narrows legacy Mobility & Materials exposure.
Majority of Mobility & Materials businesses sold to Celanese; DuPont focuses on higher-value specialty lines.
Dow and Corteva separations from DowDuPont completed; specialty products continue as DuPont de Nemours.
DowDuPont merger closes, combining Dow and DuPont before subsequent three-way split.

industry.structure: Global specialty materials is fragmented but qualification-heavy in healthcare packaging and water filtration; scale players compete on formulation, regulatory approval, and customer spec-in.
industry.share_shift: DuPont has shrunk revenue through deliberate divestitures (M&M, Delrin, Electronics) while aiming to mix toward healthcare and water; peers include 3M, Solvay, and Celanese in overlapping niches.
industry.trend: End markets favor lightweight medical packaging, water purity, and electrification-adjacent polymers; portfolio simplification and deleveraging are the dominant corporate themes post-2025 separation.
